mainEntity.name: Can a Conveyor System Be Customized to My Exact Plant Layout?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. An engineered conveyor system is laid out around your building, your machines and your product mix, using standard modules for conveying, accumulation, diverting, routing, elevation and integration. In the Avon project, a modular conveyor platform let the customer create solutions for products of different shapes, sizes and weights across two facilities, with lifts between levels.

mainEntity.name: Can a Conveyor System Integrate With My Palletizer and Case Packer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Integration is simplest when conveying, case packing and palletizing are engineered together, with accumulation placed to decouple the machines and controls that coordinate the flow. When the whole path from packaging discharge to shipping is one scope, it falls under end-of-line integration, with one partner responsible for how the machines work together.

mainEntity.name: Can a Single Supplier Engineer, Build and Install My Entire Conveyor System?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. TRF Industrial Automation engineers, builds and installs conveyor systems as part of the line, with one partner responsible for engineering, manufacturing, controls, installation and commissioning. The same scope can include case packing and palletizing. In this case, TRF designed and installed the complete automatic flow, working with a vertical transport specialist for the lifts.

mainEntity.name: How Is Vertical Transport Handled in an End-of-Line System?

acceptedAnswer.text: Lifts and elevators move product between levels without manual handling, and they are specified by load, cycle rate and footprint. In an integrated system, they are controlled as part of the same flow as the conveyors, so accumulation and routing account for the time a load spends changing levels. In this case, lifts connect levels inside the production line.
